back: Word count, mean word length, alphabetic fraction, symbol fraction, repeated trigram/line fraction. Fast and transparent; thresholds are guesses and keyword stuffing slips through.
Score documents with a small LM trained on trusted text; high perplexity means unlike the reference (spam, noise). Bias: it also removes legitimate text that differs in style.
$p=\sigma(w^\top x+b)$ with binary word-presence $x$; gradient $X^\top(p-y)/N+\lambda w$. Weights are readable; the labels define 'quality'.
Saves compute, reduces verbatim memorisation, and prevents train/validation or train/test overlap that inflates scores.
Shingles = all runs of k consecutive words. $J(A,B)=|A\cap B|/|A\cup B|$. One edited word breaks up to k shingles, so small edits cut J a lot (10% words changed, k=5: J about 0.39).
$\Pr[\min h(A)=\min h(B)]=J(A,B)$. The share of equal positions in n signatures estimates J with std $\sqrt{J(1-J)/n}$.
n = b bands x r rows. $\Pr[\text{candidate}]=1-(1-s^r)^b$; threshold near $(1/b)^{1/r}$. 16x8: 0.947 at s=0.8, 0.061 at s=0.5.
Lower similarity threshold: higher recall, more candidates, lower precision before verification. Fewer longer bands: opposite.
Normalise, shingle, MinHash, LSH bands, candidate pairs, verify with exact Jaccard, cluster (connected components), keep one per cluster. Exact dedup first via hashing normalised text.
$|G_{item}\cap G_{train}|/|G_{item}|$ over word n-grams; flag when at least tau. Use an overlap fraction, not 'any match'.

front: False positives vs false negatives in decontamination
back: Shared stock phrases (e.g. question stems) cause false positives under 'any match'. Paraphrase, translation, reordered options evade n-grams (false negatives); shorter n recovers some but adds false alarms.
$w_i\propto n_i^\alpha$. $\alpha=1$ natural proportions, $\alpha=0$ uniform. Small sources get repeated: watch epochs per source.
A mixture fixes source proportions; a curriculum changes the data order or proportions over time (e.g. more high-quality data late). Benefits are recipe-dependent: test on a proxy run.
Regexes for e-mail, phone, IPv4 (octets 0-255, look-arounds to avoid versions like 1.2.3.4.5) plus NER for names. Reduces, not eliminates, exposure.

front: Licensing and consent: what to keep
back: A manifest with source, licence/terms, crawl date, opt-outs and filters applied; document-level provenance; versioned filter code. Not legal advice: rules differ by jurisdiction and are evolving.
